blocking_findings: The regression log is red: 1 failed, 391 passed. `opensiddur/tests/exporter/test_reledmac_xslt.py:924` (`TestNotesMapping::test_a_cross_direction_instruction_still_gets_its_own_line`) expects `\OSInstructionBlock{` for an English instruction standing alone in a Hebrew div. That is exactly the case the new `xsl:when` now takes over. The output in the log does give the rubric its own paragraph (`\pend` / `\begin{english}\instructionnote{\pstart ... \pend}\end{english}` / `\pstart`), so the test's purpose ('gets its own line') is probably still met, but the assertion fails. Either update that test to state the new contract (its own `\pstart...\pend`, inside an English language scope that closes before the next Hebrew `\pstart`) or narrow the fix. Then re-run the full exporter suite and attach a clean log.
nonblocking_findings: This case no longer goes through `\OSInstructionBlock`. The new branch emits `\instructionnote{...}` directly, so any change made to `\OSInstructionBlock` in typography settings or a preamble no longer reaches standalone cross-direction rubrics in single-column streams, which is the most common case. If the macro is meant to be user-styleable, route the new paragraph through it or a sibling macro (e.g. `\OSInstructionPar`), or document the split.

The exclusion test reads `ancestor::tei:p | tei:l | tei:head` straight off the leaf. That only works because leaves are copied (losing their ancestors) only in `f:pair-heads`, when a facing stream exists, and `$has-alt-column` already excludes that. `stamp-rubric` records this information on copies for exactly this reason (`f:needs-space`, `f:parallel-block`). Any future caller that passes stamped leaves without `has-alt-column` (for example the interleaved path, if it ever pairs) would treat an inline in-paragraph rubric as standalone. Prefer the stamped attributes when present, falling back to `ancestor::`.

The new branch calls `note-content` directly instead of `apply-templates mode="emit"`, so the `note-anchor-leaves` tunnel parameter isn't passed. A rubric containing a nested editorial note could anchor or number differently than on the old path. Not exercised by any test.

Rubrics that reach the stream inside a block `j:conditional` (the comment at line 2695 says this is as common as a bare rubric) don't match `self::tei:note`, so they keep the old wrong-direction last line. That's consistent with the stated scope (standalone rubrics only), but it is a known remaining case worth a follow-up note.

Style: the new `note-lang` / `text-lang` variables are now computed for every leaf of every stream, including text nodes. It's cheap, but they could be declared inside the branch, or the test could be pulled into a function such as `f:is-cross-direction-block-rubric`, for readability. The comment is accurate and in keeping with the file.

Verified correct: `head-note-div` excludes instruction and description notes, so placing the new branch before the head-note skip branch (line 2627) cannot set a rubric twice. Any open `\pstart` is closed first, and `in-pstart` comes out false. TeX nesting is balanced: `\begin{english}{ \pstart ... \pend }\end{english}` lies entirely between paragraphs and inside `\beginnumbering`/`\begin{hebrew}`. The lualatex compile in the geometry test passed. Echoed, single-pstart, verse-aligned and alt-column streams are excluded, as stated.
limitations: Conditional coverage is thin. The new tests cover only: type="instruction", an English rubric in a Hebrew stream, entered with no `\pstart` open (the preceding `tei:p` ends with a para-break). Not tested directly: type="description"; the reverse direction (a Hebrew rubric in an English stream, i.e. the `'hebrew'` environment); entry with a `\pstart` open (the `$in-pstart` → `\pend` path); and that each exclusion keeps the old output (inside `tei:p`/`tei:l`/`tei:head`, same-direction rubric, echoed, align-verses, single-pstart, alt column). The 391 passing regression tests may cover some exclusions indirectly, but the log doesn't show which.

The geometry test disables line numbers. The rubric's paragraph is now set under the English environment, where polyglossia/reledmac's RTL state differs, so margin line-number placement for those lines (inner margin, `\leftlinenum`/`\rightlinenum`) and the keep/widow behaviour (`OSKeepAttr=3` tagging across the environment boundary) haven't been checked visually. A PDF screenshot or bbox check with line numbers enabled is still needed.

I didn't confirm whether `\instructionnote{\pstart...\pend}` (a reledmac paragraph inside a brace group) is already used elsewhere in the stylesheet. The passing lualatex run shows it compiles for this input, but not that it's safe with page breaks inside a long rubric.
